MATH 2A.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
MATH 2A.description: Math 3A with precalculus: A function approach integrating algebra, trigonometry, and differential calculus. Topics include: one-on-one and onto functions; inverse functions; properties and graphs of polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions; properties and graphs of trigonometric functions; analytic geometry; functions and limits; derivatives; techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.
MATH 2A.catalog_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.
MATH 2A.gold_rule: Math placement exam ≥ 2 or Math placement exam ≥ 3 or AP Calc AB ≥ 2 or AP Calc BC ≥ 2 or AP Calc BC (AB subscore) ≥ 2 or AP 65 ≥ 3

MATH 2B.title: Calculus with Algebra and Trigonometry
MATH 2B.description: Math 3B with precalculus: A continued review of relevant topics from precalculus (see Math 2A); integral calculus, including definite and indefinite integrals; techniques of integration, introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.
MATH 2B.catalog_text: Mathematics 2A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 3A.title: Calculus with Applications, First Course
MATH 3A.description: Differential Calculus including analytic geometry, functions and limits, derivatives, techniques and applications of differentiation; introduction to integration; logarithmic and trigonometric functions.
MATH 3A.catalog_text: Qualifying score on the Mathematics Placement Exam.
MATH 3A.gold_rule: UCSB AD ≥ 32 or AP Calc AB ≥ 2 or AP Calc BC ≥ 2 or AP Calc BC (AB subscore) ≥ 2 or Math placement exam ≥ 3 or AP 65 ≥ 4

MATH 3B.title: Calculus with Applications, Second Course
MATH 3B.description: Integral calculus including definite and indefinite integrals, techniques of integration; introduction to sequences and series; with applications in mathematics and physics.
MATH 3B.catalog_text: Mathematics 3A with a minimum grade of C.
MATH 3B.gold_rule: MATH 3A or AP Calc AB ≥ 3 or AP Calc BC (AB subscore) ≥ 3 or IB M4 ≥ 5

MATH 4A.title: Linear Algebra with Applications
MATH 4A.description: Systems of linear equations, matrix algebra, determinants, vector spaces and subspaces, basis and dimension, linear transformations, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalization, and orthogonality.
MATH 4A.catalog_text: Math 2B or 3B or 3BI with a minimum grade of C.
MATH 4A.gold_rule: MATH 2B or MATH 3B or MATH 3BI or AP Calc BC ≥ 3 or IB M ≥ 5 or IB M4 ≥ 5

MATH 4B.title: Differential Equations
MATH 4B.description: First and second order differential equations, separation of variables, linear differential equations, systems of first order equations, nonlinear differential equations and stability.
MATH 4B.catalog_text: Math 4A or Math 4AI with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 6A.title: Vector Calculus with Applications, First Course
MATH 6A.description: Calculus of functions of several variables, vector valued functions of one variable, derivative and integrals of vector functions, double and triple integrals, properties and applications of integrals, change of variables.
MATH 6A.catalog_text: Mathematics 4A (or 4AI) with a letter grade of C or better.

MATH 6B.title: Vector calculus with Applications, Second Course
MATH 6B.description: Scalar and vector fields, integration along paths, integration over surfaces and solid regions, integral theorems of vector calculus, Fourier series, partial differential equations.
MATH 6B.catalog_text: Mathematics 4B (or 4BI) and Mathematics 6A, each with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 8.title: Transition to Higher Mathematics
MATH 8.description: Introduction to the elements of propositional logic, techniques of mathematical proof, and fundamental mathematical structures, including sets, functions, relations, and other topics as time permits. Mastery of this material is essential for students planning to major in mathematics.
MATH 8.catalog_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better.
MATH 8.gold_rule: MATH 4A or MATH 4AI or MATH 4B or MATH 4BI or MATH 6A or MATH 6B

MATH 34A.title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
MATH 34A.description: Introduction to differential and integral calculus with applications to modeling in the biological sciences.

MATH 34B.title: Calculus for Social and Life Sciences
MATH 34B.description: Continued study of differential and integral calculus with differential andintegral calculus with applications. Introduction to mathematical modeling with differential equations. Calculus of several variables including an introduction to partial derivatives.
MATH 34B.catalog_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A or 34LA with a grade of C or better.
MATH 34B.gold_rule: MATH 2A or MATH 3A or MATH 34A or MATH 34LA or AP Calc AB ≥ 3 or AP Calc BC (AB subscore) ≥ 3 or AP Calc BC ≥ 3 or IB M4 ≥ 5

MATH 34LA.title: Calculus for the Life Sciences
MATH 34LA.description: Applications of differential and integral calculus to the life sciences. Includes mathematical foundations, biology examples, and computer programming to simulate dynamic systems.

MATH 34LB.title: Calculus for the Life Sciences
MATH 34LB.description: Applications of differential and integral calculus to the life sciences. Includes mathematical foundations, biology examples, and computer programming to simulate dynamic systems of more than one equation.
MATH 34LB.catalog_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A or 34LA with a grade of C or better.

MATH 94.title: Group Studies in Mathematics
MATH 94.description: Lectures and discussions on special topics. Designed for transfer students only.
MATH 94.catalog_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better.
MATH 94.gold_rule: MATH 4A or MATH 4AI or MATH 4B or MATH 4BI or MATH 6A or MATH 6B; MATH 190 [may be concurrent]

MATH 101A.title: Classical Number Systems
MATH 101A.description: A development of classical number systems starting with natural numbers and progressing through the integral, rational, real and complex number systems. Includes an introduction to number theory, mathematical induction, the fundamental theorem of arithmetic and the Euclidean algorithm. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
MATH 101A.catalog_text: Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 101B.title: Mathematical Systems
MATH 101B.description: The theory of operations within rings and fields. Polynomials, the fundamental theorem of algebra and other factorization theorems. Analyzing linear, polynomial, rational and exponential functions. Solving algebraic equations and inequalities. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
MATH 101B.catalog_text: Math 101A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 102A.title: Modern Euclidean and Noneuclidean Geometry
MATH 102A.description: Topics in plane and solid geometry. The axioms of pure, euclidean, projective, and noneuclidean geometry. Transformational geometry (isometries, dilitations, involutions, perspectivities, and projectivities). The history and the historical implications of these developments in geometry. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
MATH 102A.catalog_text: Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 102B.title: Modern Euclidean and Noneuclidean Geometry
MATH 102B.description: Topics in plane and solid geometry. The axioms of pure, euclidean, projective, and noneuclidean geometry. Transformational geometry (isometries, dilitations, involutions, perspectivities, and projectivities). The history and the historical implications of these developments in geometry. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
MATH 102B.catalog_text: Math 102A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 104A.title: Introduction Into Numerical Analysis
MATH 104A.description: Numerical methods for the solution of nonlinear equations (Newton method), for integration (quadrature formulas and composite integration), and for the initial value problem for ordinary differential equations (Euler and Kutta methods).
MATH 104A.catalog_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI, 6A, and 6B; and, Math 8 or PSTAT 8, and Math 117 and, Computer Science 5AA-ZZ or 10 or 8 or 16 or Engineering 3, each with a grade of C or above.
MATH 104A.gold_rule: (MATH 4B and MATH 6A and MATH 6B) or (MATH 4BI and MATH 6A and MATH 6B); (MATH 8 and MATH 117) or (PSTAT 8 and MATH 117); CMPSC 5* or CMPSC 10 or CMPSC 8 or CMPSC 16 or ENGR 3

MATH 104B.title: Numerical Analysis
MATH 104B.description: Numerical methods for the solution of systems of linear equations (direct and iteractive methods), and the finite difference methods for boundary value problems for (ordinary and partial) differential equations.
MATH 104B.catalog_text: Math 104A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 104C.title: Advanced Topics in Numerical Analysis
MATH 104C.description: Topics in approximation theory; numerical methods for finding eigenvalues of a matrix; and advanced topics in numerical methods for ordinary and partial differential equations.
MATH 104C.catalog_text: Math 104B with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 108A.title: Linear Algebra
MATH 108A.description: Abstract vector spaces and subspaces. Span and linear independence. Basis and dimension. Linear maps. Eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
MATH 108A.catalog_text: Math 4A and 8 each with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 108B.title: Linear Algebra
MATH 108B.description: Diagonalization, inner product spaces, projections, least-squares approximations, invariant factors and elementary divisors, canonical forms, topics from advanced matrix theory, applied linear algebra, and group representation theory.
MATH 108B.catalog_text: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 108C.title: Matrix Analysis
MATH 108C.description: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors and similarity; Unitary equivalence and normal matrices; QR factorization; Least squares; Singular Value decomposition; Moore-Penrose generalized inverse; Hermitian and symmetric matrices; Variational characterization of eigenvalues; Positive definite matrices; Nonnegative matrices; Perron-Frobenius Theorem.
MATH 108C.catalog_text: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C

MATH 111A.title: Abstract Algebra
MATH 111A.description: An introduction to group theory, focusing on finite groups. Basic algebraic concepts including homomorphisms, normal subgroups, quotients, direct products and group actions. Classification of finitely generated Abelian groups. Other topics such as semidirect products and Sylow theorems as time permits.
MATH 111A.catalog_text: Math 108A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 111B.title: Abstract Algebra
MATH 111B.description: Ring theory, ideals, factorization. Examples include number rings and polynomial rings. Module theory if time permits.
MATH 111B.catalog_text: Math 111A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 111C.title: Abstract Algebra
MATH 111C.catalog_text: Math 111B with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 113.title: Non-euclidean Geometry
MATH 113.description: An introduction to hyperbolic geometry with some discussion of other non-euclidean systems.
MATH 113.catalog_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

MATH 115A.title: Introduction to Number Theory
MATH 115A.description: Number-theoretic functions, divisibility, congruences, primitive roots and indices, quadratic residues and the quadratic reciprocity law.
MATH 115A.catalog_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

MATH 115B.title: Introduction to Number Theory
MATH 115B.description: Selected topics at the discretion of the instructor. Possibilities include (but are not limited to) Diophantine equations, the distribution of primes, number-theoretic methods in cryptography, quadratic forms, continued fractions, algebraic number theory, and partitions.
MATH 115B.catalog_text: Math 115A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 116.title: Combinatorial Analysis
MATH 116.description: Elementary counting principles, binomial coefficients, generating functions, recurrence relations, the principle of inclusion and exclusion, distributions and partitions, systems of distinct representatives, applications to computation.
MATH 116.catalog_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

MATH 117.title: Methods of Analysis
MATH 117.description: Introduction to methods of proof in analysis. topics include limits, sequences and series, continuity, compactness, as well as other topics. This course is intended to follow Mathematics 8 and to introduce students to the level of sophistication of upper-division mathematics.
MATH 117.catalog_text: Mathematics 8 or PSTAT 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

MATH 118A.title: Real Analysis
MATH 118A.description: Axioms of the real numbers, topology of metric spaces, numerical sequences, infinite series.
MATH 118A.catalog_text: Math 4B, 6A, 108A and 117, each with a minimum grade of C.
MATH 118A.gold_rule: MATH 4B and MATH 6A and MATH 108A and MATH 117

MATH 118B.title: Real Analysis
MATH 118B.description: Real functions: continuity, differentiability, Riemann integrals, power and trigonometric series.
MATH 118B.catalog_text: Math 108B and 118A, each with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 118C.title: Real Analysis
MATH 118C.description: Multivariable calculus and a selection of other topics including differential forms or Lebesgue integral.
MATH 118C.catalog_text: Math 118B with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 119A.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
MATH 119A.description: Existence, uniqueness, and stability; the geometry of phase space; linear systems and hyperbolicity; maps and diffeomorphisms.
MATH 119A.catalog_text: Mathematics 4B or 4BI and 6A with a minimum grade of C; and Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.
MATH 119A.gold_rule: (MATH 4B and MATH 6A and MATH 8) or (MATH 4BI and MATH 6A and MATH 8)

MATH 119B.title: Chaotic Dynamics and Bifurcation Theory
MATH 119B.description: Hyperbolic structure and chaos; center manifolds; bifurcation theory; and the Feigenbaum and Ruelle-Takens cascades to strange attractors.
MATH 119B.catalog_text: Mathematics 6B and Math 119A, each with a minimum grade of C

MATH 122A.title: Theory of Complex Variables
MATH 122A.description: Complex numbers, complex differentiation, analytic functions, Cauchy-Riemann equations, Taylor and Laurent series, classification of singular points, residues, evaluation of improper integrals.
MATH 122A.catalog_text: Math 6A and 8 each with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 122B.title: Theory of Complex Variables
MATH 122B.description: The argument principle, Rouche’s theorem, analytic continuation, conformal mapping, fractional transformations and applications, infinite products, harmonic functions. Other topics at the discretion of the instructor.
MATH 122B.catalog_text: Math 122A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 124A.title: Partial Differential Equations
MATH 124A.description: Introduces the derivation and solution of the fundamental linear partial differential equations (PDEs): the wave equation, the heat equation and the Laplace equation. These represent, respectively, hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic PDEs. Focuses on first and second order PDEs. Students will master methods for initial value problems (IVPs) and boundary value problems (BVPs), including the method of characteristics and the foundational techniques of the Fourier transform and potential theory, providing a rigorous basis for understanding dynamic and steady-state physical systems.
MATH 124A.catalog_text: Math 4B or 4BI, 6A, and 6B with a minimum grade of C; and Math 8 with a minimum grade of C.
MATH 124A.gold_rule: MATH 4B or MATH 4BI; MATH 6A and MATH 6B and MATH 8

MATH 124B.title: Fourier Series and Numerical Methods for PDEs
MATH 124B.description: Introduces specific solution techniques used to solve the wave, heat and Laplace equations. Focuses on separation of variables, namely Fourier series, and a variety of numerical methods. Provides students with modern methods, harmonic analysis and numerical analysis, necessary to study and solve PDEs in a variety of applications. The fast Fourier transform is studied as well as finite difference methods for parabolic and elliptic PDEs and the finite element method for elliptic boundary value problems.
MATH 124B.catalog_text: Math 4B or 4BI, and 6A, and 6B with a minimum grade of C; and 124A with a minimum grade of C.
MATH 124B.gold_rule: MATH 4B or MATH 4BI; MATH 6A and MATH 6B and MATH 124A

MATH 132A.title: Optimization
MATH 132A.description: Global and local optimization, constrained and unconstrained optimization, convex versus nonconvex optimization, Projection Theorem, linear search methods, gradient methods, Newton and Quasi-Newton methods, trust region methods.
MATH 132A.catalog_text: Math 6A and 108A, each with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 132B.title: Operations Research
MATH 132B.description: Large scale optimization, stochastic gradient descent, inexact Newton methods, limited memory BSGF, least squares problems, global optimization, optimization in general normed spaces.
MATH 132B.catalog_text: Math 132A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 137A.title: Graph and Network Theory
MATH 137A.description: Elements of graph and network theory including paths, circuits, trees, coloring, planarity, matching theory, Hall's theorem, applications to scheduling theory, flows in networks, Menger's theorem, and other topics as time permits.
MATH 137A.catalog_text: Math 4A and 8, each with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 137B.title: Spectral Graph Theory
MATH 137B.description: The graph Laplacian, eigenvalues of weighted graphs and random walks, the normalized Laplacian and Cheegers inequality, diameters and eigenvalues, expander graphs, eigenvalues of symmetric graphs, heat kernels.
MATH 137B.catalog_text: Math 108A and 137A, each with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 145.title: Introduction to Topology
MATH 145.description: Metric spaces, continuity, compactness, classification of surfaces, Euler characteristics, and fundamental groups. Additional topics at the discretion of the instructor.
MATH 145.catalog_text: Math 8 with a C or better. Either Math 108A or Math 117 with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 147A.title: Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces
MATH 147A.description: Curves and surfaces in three-dimensional Euclidean space, including Frenet formulas, signed curvature of plane curves, first and second fundamental forms, normal curvature and principal curvature, Gaussian and mean curvature, Gauss equation and Theorema Egregium, and a brief introduction to geodesics if time permits.
MATH 147A.catalog_text: Math 6A with a minimum grade of C; and Math 108A or 117 with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 147B.title: Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces
MATH 147B.description: Parallel transport, geodesics, Gauss-Bonnet Theorem, fundamental theorem of surfaces. Additional topics at the discretion of the instructor may include minimal surfaces, Codazzi equation, surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature, isothermal coordinates, and global theorems for curves.
MATH 147B.catalog_text: Math 6B and Math 147A with a minimum grade of C.

MATH 170.title: Introduction to Mathematical Finance
MATH 170.description: Describes mathematical methods for estimating and evaluating asset pricing models, equilibrium and derivative pricing, options, bonds, and the term-structure of interest rates. Also introduces finance optimization models for risk management and financial engineering.
MATH 170.catalog_text: PSTAT 120A-B and 160A, all completed with a minimum grade of C or better.

MATH 182.title: History of Mathematics
MATH 182.description: An examination of the major achievements in mathematical thinking throughout history. Topics may include the history of numerical systems in early civilizations, the development of formal proof, mathematical contributions from diverse populations and the impact of technological innovations on mathematics. Especially suitable for prospective middle and high school teachers.
MATH 182.catalog_text: Mathematics 8 with a grade of "C" or better.

MATH 190.title: Special Topics in Mathematics
MATH 190.description: An advanced treatment of mathematics content appropriate for undergraduates. The material for the course may come from algebra, geometry, analysis, applied mathematics or other areas of mathematics. Topics vary by instructor.
MATH 190.catalog_text: Math 8 with a grade of C or better.

MATH 190AI.title: Mathematical Reasonings of AI such as GPT and DeepSeek
MATH 190AI.description: This project-based course explores the mathematical reasonings of AI systems like GPT and DeepSeek. Students will work on exercises drawn from topics in Math 8, linear algebra, and calculus. For each project, the student will obtain an AI-generated solution, carefully examine it for errors, and then analyze and correct the AI's mistakes. Students will submit all project materials. Most projects will be provided by the instructor, but students will also be encouraged to find some on their own, with all projects receiving necessary instruction.
MATH 190AI.catalog_text: Math 8 with a grade of C or better.

MATH 190K.title: A First Course in Algebraic K-Theory
MATH 190K.description: An introduction to classical algebraic K-theory, focusing on the lower algebraic K-groups K0, K1, and K2 of commutative rings and their basic properties. These groups are fundamental invariants in algebra and geometry and also have connections to number theory and topology. The course explores some of these connections and known computations, and also focuses on relations with Galois cohomology, class field theory, Brauer group, and related arithmetic invariants. Prerequisites include basic knowledge of groups, rings, modules, and fields.
MATH 190K.catalog_text: basic knowledge of groups, rings, modules, and fields.
notes: basic knowledge of groups, rings, modules, and fields

MATH 190PS.title: Problem Solving
MATH 190PS.description: The Problem Solving in Mathematics course is designed to impart students with advanced problem-solving techniques and strategies in mathematics. Students will explore a diverse range of methods, including the application of parity, coloring, ordering, extremality, symmetry, invariants among others. The course emphasizes critical and creative thinking, allowing students to tackle complex mathematical challenges. Through collaboration and presentation exercises, students develop effective communication skills. The goal is to equip students with the basic abilities for research in mathematics.
MATH 190PS.catalog_text: Math 8 with a grade of C or better.

MATH 191.title: Mathematics Transition for Transfer Students
MATH 191.description: Provides transfer students with a solid mathematical foundation to ease their transition into a four-year college environment. Students will explore the fundamental axioms of integers and their properties, gaining a deep understanding of this essential mathematical concept. The curriculum extends to the study of rational numbers, real numbers, and complex numbers, emphasizing the properties and principles that underlie these numeric systems. Through a structured approach, this course equips transfer students with the mathematical knowledge and skills necessary to excel in more advanced coursework.
MATH 191.catalog_text: Mathematics 4A or 4AI or 4B or 4BI or 6A or 6B with a grade of B or better. Concurrent enrollment in Math 94.
MATH 191.gold_rule: MATH 4A or MATH 4AI or MATH 4B or MATH 4BI or MATH 6A or MATH 6B; MATH 94 [may be concurrent]

MATH 193.title: Internship in Mathematics
MATH 193.description: Faculty sponsored academic internship in industrial or research firms.

MATH 197A.title: Senior Thesis
MATH 197A.description: Independent research under the supervision of a faculty member which will result in a senior thesis. Student will concentrate on reading and gathering material for a thesis.
MATH 197A.catalog_text: Open to senior majors only; consent of department and instructor.

MATH 197B.title: Senior Thesis
MATH 197B.description: Independent research under the supervision of a faculty member which will result in a senior thesis. Student will concentrate on writing a thesis.
MATH 197B.catalog_text: Mathematics 197A. Open to senior majors only; consent of department and instructor.

MATH 199.title: Independent Studies in Mathematics
MATH 199.description: Coursework consists of academic research supervised by a faculty member on a topic not available in established course offerings.
MATH 199.catalog_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in math; consent of instructor and department.
notes: completion of 2 upper-division courses in math

MATH 199RA.title: Independent Research Assistance
MATH 199RA.description: Coursework consists of faculty supervised research assistance.
MATH 199RA.catalog_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in math; consent of instructor and department.
notes: completion of 2 upper-division courses in math

MATH 201A.title: Real Analysis
MATH 201A.description: Measure theory and integration. Point set topology. Principles of functional analysis. Lp-spaces. The Riesz representation theorem. Topics in real and functional analysis.

MATH 201B.title: Real Analysis
MATH 201B.description: Measure theory and integration. Point set topology. Principles of functional analysis. Lp-spaces. The Riesz representation theorem. Topics in real and functional analysis.

MATH 201C.title: Real Analysis
MATH 201C.description: Measure theory and integration. Point set topology. Principles of functional analysis. Lp-spaces. The Riesz representation theorem. Topics in real and functional analysis.

MATH 202A.title: Complex Analysis
MATH 202A.description: Analytic functions. Complex integration. Cauchy's theorem. Series and product developments. Entire functions. Conformal mappings. Topics in complex analysis.

MATH 202B.title: Complex Analysis
MATH 202B.description: Analytic functions. Complex integration. Cauchy's theorem. Series and product developments. Entire functions. Conformal mappings. Topics in complex analysis.

MATH 202C.title: Complex Analysis
MATH 202C.description: Analytic functions. Complex integration. Cauchy's theorem. Series and product developments. Entire functions. Conformal mappings. Topics in complex analysis.

MATH 206A.title: Matrix Analysis and Computation
MATH 206A.description: Graduate level-matrix theory with introduction to matrix computations. SVD's, pseudoinverses, variational characterization of eigenvalues, perturbation theory, direct and iterative methods for matrix computations.

MATH 206B.title: Numerical Simulation
MATH 206B.description: Linear multistep methods and Runge-Kutta methods for ordinary differential equations: stability, order and convergence. Stiffness. Differential algebraic equations. Numerical solution of boundary value problems.

MATH 206C.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations--Finite Difference Methods
MATH 206C.description: Finite difference methods for hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic PDE's, with application to problems in science and engineering. Convergence, consistency, order and stability of finite difference methods. Dissipation and dispersion. Finite volume methods. Software design and adaptivity.

MATH 206D.title: Numerical Solution of Partial Differential Equations - Finite Element Methods
MATH 206D.description: Weighted residual and finite element methods for the solution of hyperbolic, parabolic and elliptic partial differential equations, with application to problems in science and engineering. Error estimates. Standard and discontinuous Galerkin methods.

MATH 214A.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
MATH 214A.description: Existence, uniqueness, and stability; the geometry of phase space; linear systems and hyperbolicity; maps and diffeomorphisms.

MATH 214B.title: Chaotic Dynamics and Bifurcation Theory
MATH 214B.description: Hyberbolic structure and chaos; center manifolds; bifurcation theory; and the Feigenbaum and Ruelle-Takens cascades to strange attractors.

MATH 215B.title: Fourier Series and Numerical Methods
MATH 215B.description: Fourier series; generalized functions; and numerical methods.

MATH 220A.title: Modern Algebra
MATH 220A.description: Group theory, ring and module theory, field theory, Galois theory, other topics.

MATH 220B.title: Modern Algebra
MATH 220B.description: Group theory, ring and module theory, field theory, Galois theory, other topics.

MATH 220C.title: Modern Algebra
MATH 220C.description: Group theory, ring and module theory, field theory, Galois theory, other topics.

MATH 221A.title: Foundations of Topology
MATH 221A.description: Metric spaces, topological spaces, continuity, Hausdorff condition, compactness, connectedness, product spaces, quotient spaces. Other topics as time allows.

MATH 221B.title: Homotopy Theory
MATH 221B.description: Homotopy groups, exact sequences, fiber spaces, covering spaces, van Kampen Theorem.

MATH 221C.title: Differential Topology
MATH 221C.description: Topological manifolds, differentiable manifolds, transversality, tangent bundles, Borsuk-Ulam theorem, orientation and intersection number, Lefschetz fixed point theorem, vector fields.

MATH 227A.title: Advanced Topics in Geometric and Algebraic Topology
MATH 227A.description: Topics, varying from year to year, include piecewise linear and differential topology, manifolds, fiber bundles and fiber spaces, homotopy theory, and spectral sequences.

MATH 227B.title: Advanced Topics in Geometric and Algebraic Topology
MATH 227B.description: Topics, varying from year to year, include piecewise linear and differential topology, manifolds, fiber bundles and fiber spaces, homotopy theory, and spectral sequences.

MATH 227C.title: Advanced Topics in Geometric and Algebraic Topology
MATH 227C.description: Topics, varying from year to year, include piecewise linear and differential topology, manifolds, fiber bundles and fiber spaces, homotopy theory, and spectral sequences.

MATH 231A.title: Lie Groups and Lie Algebras
MATH 231A.description: Differentiable manifolds, definition and examples of lie groups, lie group-lie algebra correspondence, nilpotent and solvable lie algebras, classification of semi-simple lie algebras over the complexes, representations of lie groups and lie algebras, special topics.

MATH 231B.title: Lie Groups and Lie Algebras
MATH 231B.description: Differentiable manifolds, definition and examples of lie groups, lie group-lie algebra correspondence, nilpotent and solvable lie algebras, classification of semi-simple lie algebras over the complexes, representations of lie groups and lie algebras, special topics.

MATH 232A.title: Algebraic Topology
MATH 232A.description: Singular homology and cohomology, exact sequences, Hurewicz theorem, Poincare duality.

MATH 232B.title: Algebraic Topology
MATH 232B.description: Singular homology and cohomology, exact sequences, Hurewicz theorem, Poincare duality.

MATH 236A.title: Homological Algebra
MATH 236A.description: Algebraic construction of homology and cohomology theories, aimed at applications to topology, geometry, groups and rings. Special emphasis on hom and tensor functors; projective, injective and flat modules; exact sequences; chain complexes; derived functors, in particular, ext and tor.

MATH 236B.title: Homological Algebra
MATH 236B.description: Algebraic construction of homology and cohomology theories, aimed at applications to topology, geometry, groups and rings. Special emphasis on hom and tensor functors; projective, injective and flat modules; exact sequences; chain complexes; derived functors, in particular, ext and tor.

MATH 237A.title: Algebraic Geometry
MATH 237A.description: Affine/projective varieties, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, morphisms of varieties, rational maps, dimension, singular/nonsingular points, blowing up of varieties, tangent spaces, divisors, differentials, Riemann-Roch theorem. Special topics may include: elliptic curves, intersection numbers, Bezout's theorem, Max Noether's theorem.

MATH 237B.title: Algebraic Geometry
MATH 237B.description: Affine/projective varieties, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, morphisms of varieties, rational maps, dimension, singular/nonsingular points, blowing up of varieties, tangent spaces, divisors, differentials, Riemann-Roch theorem. Special topics may include: elliptic curves, intersection numbers,Bezout's theorem, Max Noether's theorem.

MATH 237C.title: Algebraic Geometry
MATH 237C.description: Affine/projective varieties, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, morphisms of varieties, rational maps, dimension, singular/nonsingular points, blowing up of varieties, tangent spaces, divisors, differentials Riemann-Roch theorem. Special topics may include: elliptic curves, intersection numbers, Bezout's theorem, Max Noether's theorem.

MATH 240A.title: Introduction to Differential Geometry and Riemannian Geometry
MATH 240A.description: Topics include geometry of surfaces, manifolds, differential forms, Lie groups, Riemannian manifolds, Levi-Civita connection and curvature, curvature and topology, Hodge theory. Additional topics such as bundles and characteristic classes, spin structures, and Dirac operator, comparison theorems in Riemannian geometry.

MATH 240B.title: Introduction to Differential Geometry and Riemannian Geometry
MATH 240B.description: Topics include geometry of surfaces, manifolds, differential forms, Lie groups, Riemannian manifolds, Levi-Civita connection and curvature, curvature and topology, Hodge theory. Additional topics such as bundles and characteristic classes, spin structures, and Dirac operator, comparison theorems in Riemannian geometry.

MATH 240C.title: Introduction to Differential Geometry and Riemannian Geometry
MATH 240C.description: Topics include geometry of surfaces, manifolds, differential forms, Lie groups, Riemannian manifolds, Levi-Civita connection and curvature, curvature and topology, Hodge theory. MATH CS 101A.title: Problem Solving I
MATH CS 101A.description: Discussion and solution of nonroutine mathematical problems related with different problem-solving techniques. Possible topics are: Pigeonhole principle, use of invariants and symmetries in problem solving, coloring arguments, parity, recursive arguments, extreme principle, inclusion-exclusion principle.

MATH CS 101B.title: Problem Solving II
MATH CS 101B.description: Discussion and solution of nonroutine problems in different areas of mathematics like Graph Theory, Number Theory, Combinatorics, Geometry, Game Theory, Topology, Algebra, and Analysis.

MATH CS 108A.title: Advanced Linear Algebra I
MATH CS 108A.description: An introduction to the theory of Linear Algebra with topics: Algebra of matrices, linear systems of equations, vector spaces, linear independence, basis and dimension, infinite-dimensional vectors spaces, linear transformations, matrix representation, isomorphisms, quotient spaces, dual spaces, and determinants.

MATH CS 108B.title: Advanced Linear Algebra II
MATH CS 108B.description: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, and diagonalization. Canonical form under similarity: Jordan canonical form and rational canonical form, inner product and norm. Gram-Schmidt process, adjoint of a linear operator, normal and self-adjoint operators, unitary and orthogonal operators, spectral theorem.

MATH CS 117.title: Introduction to Real Analysis
MATH CS 117.description: A rigorous introduction to the elements of analysis. Covers sequences, accumulation points, Bolzano-Weierstrass, Cauchy's criterion, the completeness property of the real number system, limits of functions, continuity, differentiability, compact sets, and the Heine-Borel theorem.

MATH CS 120.title: Special Topics in Mathematics
MATH CS 120.description: Lectures on a coherent body of mathematical topics which are not usually presented in standard mathematics courses.

MATH CS 120AI.title: Introduction to Data Science and Machine Learning: Foundations and Applications
MATH CS 120AI.description: This course provides an accessible introduction to the field of data science and related techniques from machine learning. The course will develop both mathematical foundations and theory behind learning algorithms as well as discussing practical aspects for their use in applications.

MATH CS 120BC.title: Math Book Club
MATH CS 120BC.description: A collaborative seminar on mathematical topics not ordinarily covered in the standard curriculum. Students work as a cohort under faculty supervision to study a common textbook or collection of research papers. Participants give weekly presentations, lead peer discussions, and solve related problem sets. The course emphasizes independent learning within a shared seminar setting, with focus on mathematical reading, proof analysis, problem solving, and oral communication. Topic varies by term.

MATH CS 120C.title: Special Topics in Mathematics: Combinatorics
MATH CS 120C.description: Combinatorics has its historical roots in mathematical recreations and games. Combinatorics is concerned with arrangements of the objects in a set into patterns satisfying specified rules.

MATH CS 120DA.title: Theory of Distributions and their Applications
MATH CS 120DA.description: Distributions, also known generalized functions, are objects that generalize the classical notion of functions in mathematical analysis. Distributions make it possible to differentiate functions whose derivatives do not exist in the classical sense. Distributions are widely used in the theory of partial differential equations, in physics and engineering where many problems naturally lead to differential equations whose solutions or initial conditions are singular, such as the Dirac delta function.

MATH CS 120EL.title: Special Topics in Mathematics: The Ellipse
MATH CS 120EL.description: The course delves into concepts using ellipses as a foundational shape: Synthetic & Projective geometry, theorems like Pascal's, Potential theory encompassing Newton’s cloaking, Elliptic functions aiding arc length computation, Quantization of ellipses involving Jacobi matrices, Moving boundaries (e.g., crystal growth) maintaining ellipses, with potential for broader topics.

MATH CS 120FC.title: Algebraic Combinatorics
MATH CS 120FC.description: This class discusses applications of algebra (especially linear algebra) to various combinatorial problems.

MATH CS 120FN.title: Special Topics in Mathematics: Number Systems
MATH CS 120FN.description: An exploration of basic number systems including the integers, rationals, reals, complex and beyond.

MATH CS 120FO.title: Special Topics in Mathematics - Linear Optimization
MATH CS 120FO.description: In this course, students study optimization techniques in the area of Linear Programming whose goal is to find the maximum or a minimum of a linear function subject to linear constraints. This area of mathematics has broad applications in engineering, in data analysis, in industry, in medicine, etc. The only prerequisite for this class is Linear Algebra and some Multivariable calculus.

MATH CS 120FT.title: Topology
MATH CS 120FT.description: Basic concepts in point set and algebraic topology, including compactness and fundamental groups.

MATH CS 120FV.title: Special Topics in Mathematics - Game Theory
MATH CS 120FV.description: Introduction to game theory and related topics. Includes classical game theory and combinatorial game theory up through the Sprague-Grundy Theorem.

MATH CS 120KT.title: Knot Theory
MATH CS 120KT.description: This course introduces the mathematical study of knots and links focusing on how topology, algebra, and geometry interact to distinguish and classify them. Students will learn both classical and modern knot invariants. A more apt title for this course could be 'Topics in Geometric Topology,' as we will also touch upon the importance of knots and links in the broader field of low-dimensional topology. Possible topics include the study of codimension one embeddings in manifolds, the knot group, Seifert surfaces and Seifert genus, polynomial link invariants, braids, finite and infinite cyclic coverings, the Alexander module, surgery theory, hyperbolic knot theory, and quantum invariants.

MATH CS 120PA.title: P-adic analysis and p-adic zeta functions
MATH CS 120PA.description: Introduces p-adic numbers which can be obtained by completing rational numbers with respect to an absolute value different from the usual Euclidean absolute value. Discusses p-adic analysis and a p-adic version of Riemann zeta functions.

MATH CS 120TC.title: Topological Combinatorics
MATH CS 120TC.description: Two thieves have stolen a valuable necklace made of gems of several kinds. They want to divide the necklace so that each gets the same number of each kind of gem. How many cuts do they have to make? In this course you'll learn the answer to this and other combinatorial questions and how algebraic topology is used in the proof.

MATH CS 121.title: Probability
MATH CS 121.description: This is a course on probability. It covers discrete and continuous distributions, combinatorial methods, generating functions, conditioning, the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem, stochastic processes, random walks, Brownian motion, and applications in biology, economics, engineering, and physics.

MATH CS 122A.title: Complex Variables I
MATH CS 122A.description: Covers the basics of the topology of the complex plane, series of complex numbers, differentiability of functions of a complex variable, the complex exponential and logarithm functions, contour integration, power series and analytic continuation, among other related topics.

MATH CS 122B.title: Complex Variables II
MATH CS 122B.description: Covers the basics of the topology of the complex plane, series of complex numbers, differentiability of functions of a complex variable, the complex exponential and logarithm functions, contour integration, power series and analytic continuation, among other related topics.

MATH CS 128.title: Introduction to the Higher Mathematics
MATH CS 128.description: A formal introduction to the language and culture of mathematics. Students will learn how to rigorously think about mathematics and write mathematical proofs. Topics covered include: propositional logic, set theory, cardinality, number theory, and various number systems.

MATH CS 199.title: Independent Studies
MATH CS 199.description: Serious independent study in mathematics with consenting faculty member.

PHYS 1.title: Basic Physics
PHYS 1.description: Introduction to classical mechanics for students in engineering and the physical sciences. Measurement, units, and foundations of physics; vectors; kinematics; circular motion; forces, mass, and Newton's laws; center of mass; momentum; work and energy; conservation laws; collisions; rotational kinematics.
PHYS 1.catalog_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or AP Math AB Exam with a score of 3 or better.

PHYS 2.title: Basic Physics
PHYS 2.description: Rotational dynamics and angular momentum; equilibrium and elasticity; periodic motion including LRC electrical circuits; gravitation; fluid mechanics; temperature; thermal expansion; heat and the first law of thermodynamics; heat conduction; kinetic theory of gases; entropy and the second law; heat engines.
PHYS 2.catalog_text: Physics 1 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B or AP Math BC exam with a score of 3 or better.

PHYS 3.title: Basic Physics
PHYS 3.description: Mechanical waves, wave interference and normal modes, sound and hearing, electric field, Gauss's law, electric potential, capacitance and dielectrics, current, resistance, electromotive force, DC circuits.
PHYS 3.catalog_text: Physics 2 with a grade of C- or better; Mathematics 2A-B or 3A-B (AP Math BC Exam score of 3 or better) and 4A.

PHYS 3L.title: Physics Laboratory
PHYS 3L.description: Introductory laboratory emphasizing periodic motion, sound and basic electronics.

PHYS 4.title: Basic Physics
PHYS 4.description: Magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction and inductance, AC circuits, Maxwell's equations, electromagnetic waves, light and geometrical optics, interference and diffraction.
PHYS 4.catalog_text: Physics 3 with a grade of C- or better.

PHYS 4L.title: Physics Laboratory
PHYS 4L.description: Introductory laboratory emphasizing magnetism, circuits and optics.

PHYS 5.title: Basic Physics
PHYS 5.description: Special relativity, blackbody radiation, Compton scattering, photoelectric effect, Bohr model, quantum mechanics, molecules, condensed matter, nuclear physics, elementary particles.
PHYS 5.catalog_text: Physics 4 with a grade of C- or better.

PHYS 5L.title: Physics Laboratory
PHYS 5L.description: Introductory laboratory emphasizing atomic spectra, diffraction and basic quantum physics.
PHYS 5L.catalog_text: Physics 4 or 24; and, Physics 5 or 25 (may be taken concurrently).

PHYS 6A.title: Introductory Physics
PHYS 6A.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Vectors, velocity, acceleration. Newton's laws. Work and energy. Linear momentum. Gravity. Static equilibrium. Rotational motion. Angular momentum.
PHYS 6A.catalog_text: Mathematics 2A or 3A or 34A (may be taken concurrently) or AP Math AB Exam score of 3 or better.
PHYS 6A.gold_rule: MATH 2A [may be concurrent] or MATH 3A [may be concurrent] or MATH 34A [may be concurrent] or AP Calc AB ≥ 3 or AP Calc BC (AB subscore) ≥ 3 or AP Calc BC ≥ 3 or IB M4 ≥ 5

PHYS 6AL.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
PHYS 6AL.description: Self directed laboratory course where students seek to discover simple mathematical descriptions of laws governing various physical phenomena. Each student is responsible for deciding what to measure, how to measure it, and what interpretation can be placed on the results.

PHYS 6B.title: Introductory Physics
PHYS 6B.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Oscillatory motion. Vibrations, waves, sound. Fluids. Electrostatics and DC circuits. Magnetism and magnetic forces. Induction and Faraday's law. AC circuits. If time permits: Heat and thermodynamics.
PHYS 6B.catalog_text: Physics 6A with a minimum grade of C-.
PHYS 6B.gold_rule: PHYS 6A or AP Physics C: Mech ≥ 3

PHYS 6BL.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
PHYS 6BL.description: Experiments in the mechanical, electrical and thermal properties of matter,the behavior of light, and quantum phenomena with application to the biological sciences.

PHYS 6C.title: Introductory Physics
PHYS 6C.description: Presents concepts and methodologies for understanding physical phenomena, and is particularly useful preparation for upper-division study in the life sciences. Electromagnetic waves. Geometric optics, optical instruments. Interference and diffraction. Quantum theory of the atom. Nuclear physics. If time permits: Special relativity, elementary particle physics.
PHYS 6C.catalog_text: Physics 6B with a minimum grade of C-.
PHYS 6C.gold_rule: PHYS 6B or AP Physics C: E&M ≥ 3

PHYS 6CL.title: Introductory Experimental Physics
PHYS 6CL.description: Experiments in the mechanical, electrical and thermal properties of matter,the behavior of light, and quantum phenomena with application to the biological sciences.

PHYS 7C.description: Magnetic Forces and Field, Induction, Inductance and AC circuits, Maxwell’s equations and E/M waves, Geometric and Physical Optics

PHYS 7D.title: Basic Physics
PHYS 7D.description: Temperature, Heat, Laws of Thermodynamics, Special Relativity, Photons, Wave-particle duality of Matter, Intro to Quantum Mechanics, Schrodinger Equation in 1D, Hydrogen Atom.

PHYS 7L.title: Physics Laboratory
PHYS 7L.description: Periodic motion, sound, and basic electronics, while emphasizing good laboratory techniques such as uncertainty propagation, statistical analysis, developing and testing models, and good report writing.

PHYS 8.title: Introduction to Mathematical Methods for Physics
PHYS 8.description: Single variable functions, derivatives and integrals with applications to kinematics. Taylor series. Introduction to ordinary differential equations and Newtons second law as an ODE. Vectors and scalars with physics applications. Dot and cross products. Matrices and determinants. Unit circle and trigonometric identities. Polar coordinates and kinematics in polar coordinates.

PHYS 13AL.title: Honors Introduction to Experimental Physics
PHYS 13AL.description: Covers the essence of experimental research. Students study three different systems experimentally, and write short Physical Review style articles about the results. Students are responsible for deciding what to measure, how to analyze data, what conclusions can be reached, etc.
notes: Catalog lists: Physics 3 or 23 (may be taken concurrently). GOLD enforces none.

PHYS 13BL.title: Honors Experimental Physics
PHYS 13BL.description: Computer control of experiments. Students learn LabView, and use it to measure and generate analog signals using a data acquisition card and a personal computer. Students ultimately use their computers to measure and control the temperature of a copper rod.

PHYS 13CL.title: Honors Experimental Physics
PHYS 13CL.description: Design and construction of apparatus, drafting and computer-aided design. Machine shop practice including use of all major machine tools. The class acts as a team to design and, time permitting, build a scientific apparatus for a campus research group.

PHYS 20AL.title: Experimental Physics
PHYS 20AL.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation. Basic good practices in note-taking, data collection, data visualization, error estimation, error propagation, curve fitting, and drawing conclusions, all exercised in the context of phenomena from mechanics and electronics.
PHYS 20AL.catalog_text: Physics 29 and Physics 23 (may be taken concurrently)

PHYS 20BL.title: Experimental Physics
PHYS 20BL.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation, continued. Basics of image analysis, technical drawing, additive manufacturing, oscilloscope use, searching and digesting scientific literature, as well as continued practice of skills introduced in 20AL in the context of electromagnetic and optical phenomena.
PHYS 20BL.catalog_text: Physics 20AL and Physics 24 (may be taken concurrently).

PHYS 20CL.title: Experimental Physics
PHYS 20CL.description: Introduction to Measurement and Experimentation, with an emphasis on Scientific Communication and Experimental Design. Searching the scientific literature, reading a scientific paper, proposing and executing a measurement, and formally reporting on a measurement in writing, as well as continued practice of skills introduced in 20AL and 20BL in the context of modern physics phenomena.
PHYS 20CL.catalog_text: Physics 20BL and Physics 25 (may be taken concurrently).

PHYS 21.title: General Physics
PHYS 21.description: Classical mechanics, kinematics, vectors, Newtons laws, work and energy, conservation laws, rotational kinematics.

PHYS 22.title: General Physics

PHYS 24.title: General Physics
